RadioTile.reason: Harness limitation, not a functional gap: Glimmer sets a bound `checked={{...}}` on an `<input>` as the DOM `checked` IDL property, not a reflected HTML attribute - confirmed by this addon's own `tile-group-test.gts`, which already asserts `assert.dom('input.cds--tile-input').isChecked()` (a property-based check) and passes. `normalizeElement` only inspects `el.attributes` (real attribute nodes), which can't see property-only state, so React's copy (which jsdom does reflect onto the attribute) shows as present and Ember's as absent even though both render a genuinely checked radio button.

ExpandableTile.reason: Both sides clip the collapsed tile via a real, measured inline `max-height` style (Ember's own `clipExpandableTile` modifier in tile.gts, mirroring upstream's `useIsomorphicEffect` scrollHeight measurement) - this is a harness artifact, not a missing-behavior gap. This fixture was generated in jsdom, where `scrollHeight` is always 0, so upstream's captured value here (`"0px"`) is a deterministic jsdom artifact, not a real browser measurement (see dom-parity/lib/components.mjs's top comment) - Ember's own real-Chromium test asserts the collapsed tile actually clips (a non-zero max-height, and a real height delta vs. expanded), see tile-test.gts. The `expanded` variant has no such gap - both sides clear the inline `max-height` entirely once expanded, so neither renders a style there.

Ember always wraps the below-the-fold block's yielded content in its own `<span class="cds--tile-content__below-the-fold">` (the real, styled target of @carbon/styles' opacity/visibility fade-in transition - see _tile.scss), so a caller's plain content gets the collapse fade animation for free. Upstream's ExpandableTile itself renders whatever children are passed with no such wrapper - only its own, separately-exported (and not ported here) `TileBelowTheFoldContent` sub-component adds that class, opt-in per caller. A deliberate, functional divergence (keeping the fade animation working without requiring a second sub-component this addon doesn't port), not an accidental structural gap. Applies to every variant.

Structural: @carbon/react's Checkbox renders `<input>` as a sibling of `<label>` (both direct children of the wrapper div); Ember's checkbox.gts nests the `<input>` INSIDE the `<label>` instead (a common, simpler, equally-valid HTML pattern for implicitly associating a control with its label - no `for`/`id` pairing is strictly required that way). This one tag-mismatch swallows the rest of the comparison at this position (diffing stops once tags disagree), so Ember's own nested input/label-text structure isn't cross-checked against upstream's - it's verified separately by this addon's own checkbox-test.gts instead. Ember's `checkbox.gts` has no `invalid`/`warn`/`helperText` args at all, so it never renders anything at this position - a real, larger API gap (this addon's Checkbox doesn't support upstream's invalid/warn states), out of scope for a DOM-parity-only pass. RadioButton.reason: Same harness limitation as RadioTile's entry of the same name (see that entry in this file) - Glimmer's bound `checked={{this.checked}}` sets the DOM `checked` IDL property, not a reflected HTML attribute, so `normalizeElement` (which only reads real attribute nodes) sees it as absent on the Ember side even though the radio button is genuinely checked.

RadioButtonGroup.reason: Ember's radio-button/radio-button-group.gts always renders `cds--radio-button-group--{{this.args.orientation}}` (defaulting to 'horizontal'), while @carbon/react's `RadioButtonGroup.js` only conditionally adds this class for the vertical case (`[`${prefix}--radio-button-group--${orientation}`]: orientation === 'vertical'` - it never emits a `--horizontal` variant at all, even though `orientation` defaults to 'horizontal'). Harmless either way (horizontal is the group's default flex layout regardless of this modifier class), but a real, disclosed divergence - fixing it would mean Ember's class list stops being unconditional, out of scope for a one-line fix. Applies to every variant that isn't 'vertical'.

A real, disclosed behavioral divergence: Ember's `RadioButton#labelPosition` getter falls back to `this.args.group?.args.labelPosition`, so every grouped radio button visually inherits the group's `@labelPosition`. Upstream's `RadioButtonGroup.js`'s `getRadioButtons()` never passes `labelPosition` down when cloning children (only `name`/`value`/`onChange`/`checked`/`required`) - each `RadioButton`'s own label position stays at its individual default ('right') regardless of the group's `labelPosition`, which only affects the group's own fieldset-level modifier class. This is the first (name='a') grouped RadioButton.
Same disclosed divergence as the `fieldset > div[1].classes[cds--radio-button-wrapper--label-left]` entry above, for the second (name='b') grouped RadioButton.

A real, disclosed divergence, not a markup bug: upstream's `getRadioButtonsWithWrappers`-style cloning (`RadioButtonGroup.js`) only ever passes `name`/`value`/`onChange`/`checked`/`required` down to each child `RadioButton` - never `disabled` - relying entirely on the surrounding `<fieldset disabled>` to actually disable the inputs. Ember's `RadioButton#disabled` getter falls back to `this.args.group?.args.disabled`, so a grouped input gets an explicit `disabled` attribute in addition to inheriting it from the fieldset. Functionally identical either way (`fieldset[disabled]` already makes every descendant control unfocusable regardless of its own `disabled`/`tabindex`), matching the same call already made for RadioTile/TileGroup - see AGENTS.md's own note on this. Toggle.reason: @carbon/react's Toggle links its `<button role="switch">` to its own label via `aria-labelledby={ariaLabelledby ?? Ember's `toggle.gts` has no equivalent wiring - the button and the visible label text are never connected via ARIA at all, even though `@name` is Ember's direct analog of `labelText`. A real, disclosed accessibility gap (screen readers get no accessible name from the label association upstream provides), out of scope for a DOM-parity-only pass. Applies to every variant.

ProgressBar.reason: Harness artifact of upstream's own quirky indeterminate math, not a missing Ember feature worth reproducing: @carbon/react's `useIsomorphicEffect` always computes `percentage = (cappedValue ?? NaN) / max` and sets `ref.current.style.transform = 'scaleX(' + percentage + ')'` whenever the bar isn't finished/error - with no value passed (the indeterminate case), this literally becomes the broken CSS value `scaleX(NaN)`, which has no visual effect in a real browser. Ember's `{{if @value ...}}` guard simply omits the `style` attribute entirely when `@value` is absent, which is the more sensible behavior; reproducing upstream's `NaN` output here would mean intentionally copying its own bug.

Ember's `progress-indicator.gts` has no equivalent - a harmless React-only quirk, not a real feature to reproduce. Applies to every variant.

The Ember port wraps it in an out-of-flow, visually hidden role="cell" <div>, so the row only owns cells and no visible column is added. Tabs.reason: Ember's yielded `TabPane` renders `tabindex="0"` on its panel; the pinned `@carbon/react`'s `TabPanel` renders none. Left as-is: it only makes the panel itself focusable, which the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern recommends when a panel has no focusable content of its own, and removing it would silently change keyboard behaviour for existing consumers - a real, deliberate-looking divergence rather than a markup slip.
